articles.title: Keralam Messi Gate: SIT questions former minister V Abdurahman over Spain visit, sponsor selection and stadium handover
articles.description: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) recorded the statement of former Sports Minister V. Abdurahman in connection with his Spain visit and the selection of the sponsor for the proposed footballer Lionel Messi’s tour to the state. There were allegations of financial irregularities pertaining to the promise to bring Lionel Messi and the Argentina team to Kerala. Reportedly, the interrogation took place earlier this week and lasted nearly four hours. The questioning was based on the former minister’s Spain visit and the manner in which Anto Augustine, Managing Director of Reporter Broadcasting Company, was selected as the sponsor, the intervention of the minister’s office in the process and the documents collected during raids at the offices of Reporter Broadcasting Company and the residence of Anto Augustine, one of the major accused in the Messi Gate case. The other day, the SIT examined the e-mail correspondence between the minister’s office, the Argentina Football Association and the sponsor. The minister’s statement was recorded on the basis of these documents and the questionnaire prepared by the SIT. There are reports that the minister’s correspondence was copied to Anto Augustine. Earlier, there were reports that questions had arisen regarding the procedures followed for selecting Reporter Broadcasting Company and Anto Augustine as sponsors for bringing the Argentina team and Messi to Kerala. The SIT is also inquiring into the selection of the sponsors without following tender procedures. The SIT is looking into the alleged intervention of the minister’s office in handing over the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, Kochi, to Anto Augustine for conducting the football match. According to reports, the related documents have been examined, along with the allegation that there was unusual intervention in handing over the stadium to Anto Augustine. The SIT will also examine whether the allegation that the former minister had granted unjustified support to Anto Augustine is true. Cheating and conspiracy are the allegations against Anto Augustine and Reporter Broadcasting Company. Various documents and electronic devices are being examined in connection with the case. The financial aspects of the case have also come under scrutiny. Around ₹126 crore was reportedly transferred by Reporter Broadcasting Company to a foreign entity in two instalments in 2025. The proposed project was estimated to involve around ₹210 crore in expenditure, while the Argentina Football Association match fee was reportedly estimated at ₹198 crore. The financial inquiry also identified suspected GST evasion of ₹25.78 crore in transactions linked to the proposed event. Of this, ₹22.68 crore reportedly relates to non-payment of IGST under the Reverse Charge Mechanism. The total GST demand, including tax, penalty and interest, could reportedly reach around ₹56.32 crore. Also Read: Keralam Messi-gate: Rs 126 cr deal widens into Rs 549.22 cr fraud; SIT seeks ED probe into ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan Questions have also been raised over financial transactions of around ₹200 crore through accounts associated with Anto Augustine and Reporter Broadcasting Company. The transactions and the explanation given for them are being examined. Abdurahman’s Spain visit, for which the government reportedly spent ₹13 lakh, has also come under scrutiny. Questions have been raised over the arrangements made for the proposed Argentina-Messi event and the use of government resources in connection with it. The case has now taken a further turn, with reports that the SIT has recommended registration of a case against the former minister under the Prevention of Corruption Act over alleged misuse of official position. Messi Gate has become an insult to the injury for the CPM-led Left Democratic Front and its supremo and former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan. Pinarayi Vijayan is already under pressure over the CMRL-Exalogic case, in which his daughter Veena Vijayan and her husband and former minister P. A. Mohammed Riyas are allegedly involved.

articles.title: MHI approves 382 sites for EV charging infrastructure in Delhi
articles.description: MHI approved 382 EV charging sites in Delhi, identified by the Revenue Dept and DTC. These sites were reassessed for segment-wise deployment, with a tender for 160-180 sites to be floated soon.

articles.title: Russia’s Pivot to Asia: TNF 2026 expands Moscow’s energy technology drive across Asian and global markets
articles.description: The XI International Industrial and Energy Forum (TNF 2026), held in Tyumen from September 14-17, marked a significant expansion of Russia’s industrial and energy-technology agenda. For the first time, TNF operated with full international status, positioning the forum as a platform connecting Russian oil-and-gas producers, technology companies, equipment manufacturers, universities and government institutions with foreign energy markets. More than 18,000 participants from over 60 Russian regions attended, with approximately 80 per cent representing senior executives from the fuel-and-energy complex and related industries. Major participants included Gazprom, Gazprom Neft, LUKOIL, NOVATEK, Surgutneftegaz and leading oilfield-service companies. International participation included Kazakhstan’s KazMunayGas and QazaqGaz, Belarusian companies, China, Vietnam, Iran, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan and the UAE’s ADNOC. More than 50 cooperation agreements, over 200 technology launches and more than 200 business meetings were reported by ‘Russia’s Pivot To Asia’. TNF’s internationalization represents an expansion from 2025, when approximately 15,000 participants, 1,500 companies and three foreign delegations attended. The 2026 forum placed greater emphasis on international supplier qualification, technology exports, localization and industrial cooperation. The central economic challenge discussed at TNF was Russia’s increasing dependence on technologies for hard-to-recover oil reserves. More than half of Russia’s oil reserves are classified as hard to recover, while roughly 30 per cent of 2026 production is associated with such resources. Oil production with condensate is projected at approximately 511 million tonnes in 2026, with Ministry of Economic Development baseline projections reaching 516 million tonnes in 2027 and 525 million tonnes in 2028–2029. Russia’s oil-and-gas equipment localization rate reached approximately 80 per cent by the end of 2025, with a target of 90 per cent by 2030 and an estimated 82 per cent in 2026. The domestic oil-and-gas machinery market reached ₽294 billion in H1 2026 and could approach ₽800 billion for the full year. A roadmap covering 220 critical technologies has identified solutions for 170 positions; 55 technologies are reportedly in serial production, 56 are undergoing prototype testing and more than 80 R&D projects remain active. Also Read: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: 16 killed, 30 injured as suicide attacker rams against joint check post in Dera Ismail Khan ‘Russia’s Pivot To Asia’ said that technology priorities included drilling automation, enhanced oil recovery, domestic polymers and chemicals, industrial software, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital twins, robotics, unmanned monitoring, autonomous field systems, offshore technologies and energy infrastructure. Gazprom Neft and Tyumen State University expanded cooperation in robotics, permafrost production, intelligent monitoring, enhanced recovery and autonomous operations. International cooperation increasingly focused on creating joint technology chains rather than simply exporting finished equipment. Kazakhstan provided a concrete energy-trade dimension: its planned Gazprom gas purchases were approximately 11 bcm in 2026, compared with 4 bcm in 2025, while around 9 bcm was being discussed for 2027. Russia and Kazakhstan are also developing the Ishim-Astana pipeline, potentially enabling Russian gas supplies of up to 6.3 bcm annually. China remains a major energy market. During January–August 2026, Chinese imports of Russian LNG reached 5.15 million tonnes, up 28.2 per cent year-on-year, while oil imports reached 77.65 million tonnes, up 18.1 per cent. Russian LNG imports were valued at US$2.66 billion and oil imports at US$44.84 billion. The UAE offered another important route through ADNOC’s supplier-qualification process. Russian authorities reported positive technical conclusions for 60 INTI standards, with eight Russian manufacturers pre-qualified and seven undergoing qualification. Additional opportunities were identified in Belarus, Iran, Vietnam, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Algeria, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Bangladesh, particularly in drilling, gas infrastructure, digitalization, equipment localization, oilfield services and energy projects. Bangladesh’s 2026 tender for 26 offshore oil-and-gas blocks, with bids due November 30, provides a potential additional avenue for Russian participation. The strategic significance of TNF 2026 therefore lies in its attempt to transform Russian import substitution into export-oriented industrial cooperation. The emerging model combines Russian engineering, software, drilling and difficult-field expertise with foreign manufacturing capacity, financing, certification, local servicing and market access. The longer-term measure of success will be whether TNF agreements develop into serial production, joint ventures, technology licensing, localization, international certification, sustained service contracts and increased Russian technology exports.
